title: Normalization commutes with completion away from the special fibre
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with completion $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X	o\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and put $Y=X	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a scheme $W$, write $W^
u	o W$ for its normalization: the disjoint union of the function-field normalizations of the irreducible components of $W$ with their reduced structures [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. If the complement of the special fibre (the inverse image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A)$) in $Y$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then the normalization $X^
u	o X$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and its base change $X^
u	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A)	o Y$ is isomorphic over $Y$ to the normalization $Y^
u	o Y$.

proof.text: Choose an affine cover of $X$ by opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite-type $A$-algebra, as supplied by local finite type, and work on one such open, and put $C=B\otimes_A\widehat A$, $I=\mathfrak mB$. The affine fibre-product formula gives the corresponding open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset Y$. The completion $\widehat A$ is Noetherian and local, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, and it is complete: apply module-completion completeness to $M=A$, noting that $\mathfrak m^n\widehat A=(\mathfrak m\widehat A)^n$. Thus the complete-local Nagata theorem makes $\widehat A$ Nagata. Local completion is faithfully flat, so its base change $B\to C$ is faithfully flat. Both $B$ and $C$ are Noetherian by finite-type Noetherianity. Moreover $B/I\cong C/IC$, by tensoring the completion residue-field isomorphism with $B$. The special fibre in this chart is exactly $V(IC)$.

proof.text: The base-change map $D\to D\otimes_B C$ is faithfully flat. Its target is the normal ring $C^{\nu}$, so normality descent makes $D$ normal. This uses the ring version, not the narrower field-extension descent statement. Since a finite algebra is finite type (its module generators also generate it as an algebra), finite-type Noetherianity makes $D$ Noetherian. Thus $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ is normal and locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0BG9 (lemma-normalization-completion), last paragraph: normality of the algebraized finite scheme

proof.text: Every minimal prime $\mathfrak t$ of $D$ contracts to a minimal prime of $B$. Indeed faithful flatness of $D\to C^{\nu}$ gives a prime above $\mathfrak t$; choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak u$ inside it. Its contraction is still $\mathfrak t$, by minimality of $\mathfrak t$. The normalization-properties node says that $\mathfrak u\cap C$ is minimal in $C$. A minimal prime under a flat map contracts to a minimal prime: if a strictly smaller prime existed below its contraction, going down would give a strictly smaller prime upstairs. Apply this to $B\to C$. This proves the claim even for components wholly inside the special fibre.

source.place: Tag 0BG9 (lemma-normalization-completion), last sentence: verification of the component-dominance needed to identify X prime with normalization

proof.text: Fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B$. Faithful flatness gives a prime of $C$ over it; a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ contained in that prime still contracts to $\mathfrak p$. Put $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $L=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $E=D\otimes_B K$. These are fields $K\subseteq L$ and a finite $K$-algebra $E$. The generic-fibre assertion for normalization gives, as $L$-algebras, $E\otimes_K L=D\otimes_B L\cong C^{\nu}\otimes_C L\cong L$. Therefore the unit map $K\to E$ is an isomorphism: after tensoring with the field extension $L/K$ it is an isomorphism, and a nonzero kernel or cokernel would remain nonzero on scalar extension, as is seen from a vector-space basis. Thus $E=K$. Primes of this fibre are precisely primes of $D$ over $\mathfrak p$, so there is exactly one, with residue field $K$. It is minimal: a minimal prime beneath it contracts to a minimal prime of $B$ by the previous step, necessarily $\mathfrak p$, and uniqueness forces equality. Together with the preceding step this proves a bijection of generic points and isomorphisms of their residue fields.

source.place: Tag 0BG9 (lemma-normalization-completion), last sentence: missing generic-field check in the identification with normalization

proof.text: The finite morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is integral, $Z$ is normal and locally Noetherian, and the previous two steps prove exactly the generic-point and residue-field hypotheses of normalization recognition. Consequently the recognition clause gives a unique isomorphism $Z\cong(\operatorname{Spec}B)^\nu$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B$. It follows that this normalization is finite and that its base change is $\operatorname{Spec}C^{\nu}$, with the prescribed structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}C$. No reducedness of $B$ has been assumed: recognition applies to the reductions at the generic points.

source.place: Tag 0BG9 (lemma-normalization-completion), last sentence: identification of X prime as normalization

proof.text:
Finally normalization restricts to normalization on open subschemes. Therefore the finite normalization maps just obtained on affine opens of $X$ are restrictions of $X^
u	o X$, proving its finiteness since finiteness is local on the target. The comparison isomorphisms on the corresponding opens of $Y$ agree on overlaps: each identifies the componentwise normalization and is the identity on its generic residue fields; the uniqueness in normalization recognition makes the two overlap identifications equal. The maps therefore glue: their underlying continuous maps agree on an open cover, and the maps of structure sheaves glue section by section by the sheaf axiom; their inverse maps glue in the same way. This gives an isomorphism $X^
u	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A\cong Y^
u$ over $Y$.
